baslik: The Bridge That Fell With a Train on It
sonuc: collapsed in a storm while a train crossed
tetik: a winter gale hitting a lightly built girder span
mekanizma: wind loading the designer never allowed for, acting on weak cast-iron column lugs
ders: British bridges were afterwards designed for explicit wind pressure
zincir: SPAN AND TRAIN FALL INTO THE TAY
yanilgi: The train did not simply blow off the rails. The bridge itself failed: its columns and their cast-iron fixings could not resist the storm.
tartisma: The designer was knighted months before the collapse. How much should one engineer's reputation carry?
basliklar: Why the Tay Bridge Collapsed
The Storm Nobody Designed For
soru: Would you have crossed that night?
sahneler: In a winter storm, a bridge in Scotland fell with a train on it.
The high girders collapsed, and everyone aboard was killed.
Investigators found the bridge was never designed for wind.
Its columns were held by weak cast-iron lugs.
Many were badly made and poorly inspected.
The gale pushed on the girders and the train together.
The columns gave way, and the span dropped into the Tay.
After that, British bridges had to be designed for wind.

baslik: The Iron Girder That Snapped Under a Passing Train
sonuc: broke as a train passed over it
tetik: extra ballast laid on a cast-iron girder bridge
mekanizma: cast iron failing in tension, likely aided by torsion from the girder's design
ders: cast-iron girders for railway bridges were abandoned after a Royal Commission
zincir: CAST IRON USED FOR LONG GIRDERS
yanilgi: Wrought-iron ties were added to strengthen the cast-iron girders, but they did not make a brittle material safe under tension.
tartisma: The bridge had passed its inspection. Is passing a test the same as being safe?
basliklar: Why the Dee Bridge Failed
The Brittle Iron That Broke Railway Engineering
sahneler: A railway bridge in Chester broke as a train crossed it.
The girder snapped, and carriages crashed into the River Dee.
The girders were made of cast iron.
Cast iron is strong when squeezed but brittle when stretched.
Days earlier, extra ballast had been laid on the deck.
That added load pushed a girder past its limit.
A Royal Commission studied the use of iron in railways.
Cast-iron girders were then abandoned for railway bridges.

baslik: The Iron Bridge That Gave Way in a Blizzard
sonuc: collapsed under a train in a snowstorm
tetik: a fatigue crack in a cast-iron lug of the truss
mekanizma: fatigue fracture of a cast-iron angle block in an experimental iron truss
ders: the disaster pushed railways toward independent bridge design review
yanilgi: The cold didn't break the bridge on its own. A flaw in one cast-iron block had been growing for years.
tartisma: The design came from the railway's own president, and engineers had doubts. Who reviews the boss's design?
basliklar: Why the Ashtabula Bridge Collapsed
The Flaw Growing Inside an Iron Bridge
sahneler: In a blizzard, an iron railway bridge in Ohio gave way.
The train plunged into the ravine, and its stoves set the wreck on fire.
The bridge used an experimental iron truss.
One cast-iron block in it carried a hidden flaw.
Every passing train made that crack a little longer.
That night, the weakened truss finally broke.
Engineers had doubted the design for years.
It pushed railways toward independent review of bridge designs.

baslik: A Ship in a Storm Knocked Down a Bridge
sonuc: lost a main span when a freighter hit it
tetik: a freighter blinded by a squall striking a pier
mekanizma: ship impact on an unprotected support pier
ders: the replacement bridge was built with massive pier-protection islands
yanilgi: The bridge wasn't weak. Its piers were simply never protected from a ship that left the channel.
tartisma: Drivers kept going over the gap because they couldn't see it. How should a bridge warn traffic it has fallen?
basliklar: Why the Sunshine Skyway Collapsed
The Freighter That Took Down a Bridge
soru: Would you have seen the gap?
sahneler: A freighter slammed into a support pier of Florida's Sunshine Skyway.
A main span fell into Tampa Bay, and thirty five people were killed.
A sudden squall had blinded the ship's pilot.
The freighter drifted out of the channel.
The piers had no protection against a ship.
In the rain, drivers couldn't see the missing span.
Several vehicles drove straight off the edge.
The new bridge sits behind huge concrete islands that stop ships.

baslik: A Ship Lost Power — and a Bridge Fell in Seconds
sonuc: collapsed after a container ship hit a pier
tetik: a container ship losing electrical power in the channel
mekanizma: ship impact on an unprotected main-span pier of a continuous truss
ders: US ports began reassessing pier protection on bridges over shipping channels
yanilgi: The bridge didn't fail by being old or weak. A continuous truss can't survive losing a main pier, and nothing kept the ship away from it.
tartisma: The ship's mayday gave police time to stop traffic. How much warning does a bridge need?
basliklar: Why the Key Bridge Collapsed
The Blackout on a Ship That Dropped a Bridge
sahneler: In Baltimore, a container ship struck a pier of the Key Bridge.
Within seconds the main spans collapsed into the river.
The ship had lost electrical power as it left port.
Without power, it drifted toward a support pier.
That pier held up a continuous steel truss.
Once it was hit, the whole structure unzipped.
A mayday call let police stop traffic just in time.
Ports began rechecking how bridge piers are protected from ships.

baslik: The Hidden Cables Inside Genoa's Collapsed Bridge
sonuc: collapsed during a storm in Genoa
tetik: corroded steel tendons hidden inside concrete stays
mekanizma: corrosion of prestressing tendons encased in concrete stays that could not be inspected
ders: Italy launched a national inspection campaign for ageing bridges
zincir: WATER AND SALT REACH THE STEEL
yanilgi: The storm wasn't the cause. The steel inside the concrete stays had been corroding for years where nobody could see it.
tartisma: Its own designer warned about corrosion decades earlier. Why do warnings about ageing structures get postponed?
basliklar: Why the Morandi Bridge Collapsed
The Corrosion You Couldn't See
soru: How do you inspect what you can't see?
sahneler: A motorway bridge in Genoa collapsed during a storm.
Cars and trucks fell with it, and forty three people died.
The bridge hung from concrete stays.
Inside them were steel tendons carrying the load.
Water and salt reached that steel and corroded it.
The concrete hid the damage from inspectors.
When one stay failed, the span and tower fell.
Italy then launched a national campaign to inspect ageing bridges.

baslik: A Rusted Pin Dropped a Section of Interstate 95
sonuc: dropped a section of Interstate 95 into the river
tetik: rust forcing a hanger off its pin
mekanizma: corrosion pack-out pushing a pin-and-hanger assembly off its pin
ders: pin-and-hanger bridges were retrofitted and inspected far more closely
yanilgi: No truck overloaded it. Rust built up so much that it physically pushed a hanger off its pin.
tartisma: The critical pin was hard to see during inspections. Should hard-to-inspect details be allowed in new designs?
basliklar: Why the Mianus River Bridge Collapsed
The Rust That Pushed a Bridge Apart
sahneler: At night, a section of Interstate 95 dropped into a Connecticut river.
Vehicles fell with it, and three people were killed.
The span hung from steel hangers held by pins.
Blocked drains let water sit on the steel.
Rust built up behind one hanger until it pushed sideways.
The hanger slid off its pin, and the span fell.
Nobody could easily see that pin during inspections.
Bridges with this detail were retrofitted and inspected more closely.

baslik: The Flood That Dug Away a Bridge's Foundation
tetik: floodwater scouring the soil under a pier
mekanizma: scour undermining a spread footing that lacked adequate riprap protection
ders: scour became a required part of US bridge inspections
yanilgi: The water didn't knock the bridge over. It quietly dug the ground out from under one pier.
tartisma: Scour happens underwater, where inspectors rarely look. How do you inspect a riverbed?
basliklar: Why the Schoharie Creek Bridge Collapsed
The Invisible Hole Under a Bridge
sahneler: A New York Thruway bridge collapsed into a flooded creek.
Cars drove into the gap, and ten people were killed.
The pier had not been hit or overloaded.
The flood dug away the soil beneath its foundation.
Engineers call this scour.
The stones meant to protect the footing had worn away.
With nothing under it, the pier tipped and the spans fell.
Scour checks then became a required part of bridge inspection.

baslik: Sand Mining Undermined a Bridge Until It Fell
sonuc: collapsed into the Douro River with a bus on it
tetik: years of sand extraction lowering the riverbed
mekanizma: pier foundation undermined by riverbed erosion accelerated by sand extraction
ders: Portugal reviewed river sand extraction and bridge foundation inspections
yanilgi: The flood only finished the job. Years of dredging had already removed the ground that held up a pier.
tartisma: The dredging was legal. Should one industry be allowed to weaken another's infrastructure?
basliklar: Why the Hintze Ribeiro Bridge Collapsed
The Riverbed That Disappeared
sahneler: A bridge over Portugal's Douro River collapsed at night.
A bus and cars fell into the river, and fifty nine people were killed.
The cause started years before.
Sand was dredged from the river for construction.
The riverbed dropped, exposing a pier's foundation.
A winter flood washed away what support was left.
The pier gave way, and the spans followed.
Portugal then reviewed sand extraction and foundation checks.

baslik: Bad Welds Dropped a Span Into Seoul's Han River
sonuc: dropped a span into the Han River at rush hour
tetik: faulty welds in the suspended truss
mekanizma: fatigue cracking at poorly welded connections of a suspended truss span
ders: South Korea overhauled bridge inspection and maintenance rules
yanilgi: It wasn't a single overloaded truck. Weak welds had been cracking under years of traffic.
tartisma: The bridge was only fifteen years old. How do you prove construction quality after the fact?
basliklar: Why the Seongsu Bridge Collapsed
The Welds That Failed Under Rush Hour
sahneler: During the morning rush, a span of Seoul's Seongsu Bridge fell into the river.
A bus and cars plunged with it, and thirty two people died.
The failure started in its welds.
Connections in the steel truss had been poorly welded.
Traffic grew heavier than the design expected.
Year after year, fatigue cracks spread from the bad welds.
Then one connection let go.
South Korea overhauled how its bridges are inspected and maintained.

baslik: The Bridge That Was Cracking Before It Fell
sonuc: collapsed onto traffic days after being lifted into place
tetik: cracks at one truss node while workers re-tensioned a rod
mekanizma: design error at a diagonal-to-deck connection, overstressed during re-tensioning
ders: engineers must act on structural cracks before letting work continue above traffic
zincir: CRACKS JUDGED NOT A SAFETY ISSUE
yanilgi: The cracks were seen and reported before the collapse. They were judged not to be a safety concern.
tartisma: The road below stayed open while work continued. When should cracks close a road?
basliklar: Why the FIU Pedestrian Bridge Collapsed
The Cracks They Saw and Kept Working
sahneler: A new pedestrian bridge in Miami collapsed onto busy traffic.
Cars were crushed beneath it, and six people were killed.
Days earlier, cracks had appeared at one end.
They were reported, then judged not to be a safety issue.
The connection there had been designed too weak.
Workers re-tensioned a rod in that spot, above open lanes.
The cracked node broke, and the span fell.
Now cracks like these are supposed to stop work and close the road.

baslik: A Bridge Span Fell During Construction — and Changed Box Girders
tetik: a buckle corrected by removing bolts from a splice
mekanizma: buckling of a steel box-girder span during erection, worsened by bolt removal
ders: box-girder design and erection rules were rewritten after a Royal Commission
yanilgi: The span wasn't finished and loaded. It failed while crews were trying to fix a buckle in the steel.
tartisma: Removing the bolts seemed like a normal fix. How do you know when a repair makes things worse?
basliklar: Why the West Gate Bridge Collapsed
The Bolts They Removed Before the Collapse
sahneler: A huge steel span of Melbourne's West Gate Bridge collapsed during construction.
It crushed the site huts below, and thirty five workers were killed.
The span had been assembled in two halves.
They didn't line up, and a buckle formed in the steel.
To flatten it, crews removed bolts from a joint.
That weakened the span, and the buckle spread.
The whole section fell to the ground.
A Royal Commission rewrote the rules for building box girders.

baslik: Marching Soldiers and a Storm Snapped a Suspension Bridge
tetik: soldiers crossing in step during a storm
mekanizma: oscillation from wind and marching troops on corroded suspension cables
ders: suspension bridges in France were restricted and cable anchorages inspected
yanilgi: Marching alone didn't destroy it. Wind, marching troops and corroded cables combined on the same day.
tartisma: The soldiers had been told to break step, but the deck was already swaying. Can one rule prevent resonance?
basliklar: Why the Angers Bridge Collapsed
The Bridge That Swayed Under an Army
sahneler: A suspension bridge in Angers collapsed under a column of soldiers.
The deck plunged into the river, and two hundred twenty six soldiers died.
A storm was already shaking the bridge.
As troops crossed, the deck began to sway.
Each step pushed it further.
The cables were corroded where they were anchored.
One gave way, and the deck fell.
France restricted suspension bridges and inspected their cables.

baslik: The Rusted Legs Under a Pittsburgh Bridge
sonuc: collapsed hours before a presidential visit
tetik: legs corroded through after years of clogged drainage
mekanizma: section loss from corrosion in the steel legs of a rigid-frame bridge
ders: inspection findings now require load re-rating and follow-up when section loss is found
yanilgi: The damage wasn't hidden. Inspectors had recorded the corrosion and clogged drains for years.
tartisma: The problem was written down in reports. Why does a known defect stay unfixed?
basliklar: Why the Fern Hollow Bridge Collapsed
The Corrosion Written Down for Years
sahneler: Early one morning, a Pittsburgh bridge collapsed into a ravine.
A bus and cars fell with it, but nobody died.
The bridge stood on slender steel legs.
Clogged drains had soaked them with water and debris.
Over years, the steel rusted through.
Inspectors had written it down again and again.
Finally one leg buckled, and the frame came down.
Now findings like these must trigger a new load rating and repairs.

baslik: The Double-Deck Freeway That Pancaked in an Earthquake
sonuc: collapsed onto its lower deck in an earthquake
tetik: shaking amplified by soft soil under the viaduct
mekanizma: shear failure of non-ductile concrete columns connecting the two decks
ders: California retrofitted its freeway structures for ductility
yanilgi: Older freeways weren't all destroyed. This one stood on soft bay mud and had brittle column joints.
tartisma: It met the codes of its time. When should old structures be forced up to new codes?
basliklar: Why the Cypress Viaduct Collapsed
The Freeway That Fell On Itself
soru: Would you drive the lower deck?
sahneler: In an earthquake, Oakland's double-deck freeway collapsed onto itself.
The top deck crushed cars below, and forty two people died.
It stood on soft mud near the bay.
That mud amplified the shaking.
The concrete columns had too little steel to bend.
They cracked and sheared instead.
Section after section of upper deck came down.
California then retrofitted its freeways to bend, not break.

baslik: The Ship That Cut a City in Half
sonuc: lost spans when a bulk carrier hit its piers
tetik: a bulk carrier pushed off course by the current
mekanizma: ship impact on unprotected piers outside the navigation span
ders: shipping rules around the bridge were tightened and traffic was stopped for passing ships
yanilgi: The ship didn't hit the channel span. It struck piers nearby that were never meant to face a ship.
tartisma: Hobart was cut in two for years. How much redundancy should one bridge city have?
basliklar: Why the Tasman Bridge Collapsed
The Night Hobart Was Cut in Two
sahneler: A bulk carrier crashed into the piers of Hobart's Tasman Bridge.
Two spans fell onto the ship, and it sank.
The current had pushed it off course.
It struck piers that were never meant to face a ship.
In the dark, cars drove into the gap.
Twelve people died that night.
The city was split in two for years.
Ships and traffic were then kept apart whenever vessels passed.

baslik: Why London's New Bridge Started Swaying Under Walkers
sonuc: began swaying under crowds on opening day
tetik: thousands of pedestrians adjusting their steps to the sway
mekanizma: synchronous lateral excitation: walkers falling into step with the bridge's sideways motion
ders: footbridge design now checks for lateral crowd-induced vibration
yanilgi: It wasn't soldiers marching or wind. Ordinary walkers unconsciously fell into step with a small sideways sway.
tartisma: The effect wasn't in the design codes. How do engineers design for something nobody has measured?
basliklar: Why the Millennium Bridge Wobbled
The Crowd That Made a Bridge Sway
sahneler: On opening day, London's new Millennium Bridge began to sway.
Within minutes, the deck was swaying so much that people clung to the rails.
The cause was the people walking on it.
A small sideways sway made walkers widen their steps.
Without noticing, they fell into step together.
Each step pushed the bridge further, and the sway grew.
Engineers added dampers to absorb the motion.
Footbridges are now checked for this crowd effect.

baslik: A Lost Barge Bent a Rail Bridge Minutes Before a Train
sonuc: derailed a passenger train into a bayou
tetik: a towboat lost in fog pushing a barge into the bridge
mekanizma: barge impact displacing a span and kinking the track without breaking the signal circuit
ders: towboats got radar training requirements and bridges near waterways got better protection
yanilgi: The signal system didn't fail to detect a broken rail. The rail was bent, not broken, so the circuit stayed complete.
tartisma: The pilot didn't know he had hit a bridge. How do you report an accident you don't know happened?
basliklar: Why the Sunset Limited Crashed at Big Bayou Canot
The Bent Rail the Signals Couldn't See
soru: How do you detect a bent rail?
sahneler: An Amtrak train plunged off a bridge into an Alabama bayou.
Carriages sank and burned, and forty seven people died.
Minutes earlier, a barge had hit the bridge in thick fog.
The towboat pilot didn't realize it was a railway bridge.
The impact bent the track out of line.
But the rails didn't break, so the signals stayed green.
The train reached the kink at full speed.
Towboat crews then had to be trained to use their radar.

baslik: Why Soldiers Break Step on Bridges
tetik: soldiers marching in step across the deck
mekanizma: rhythmic loading from marching exciting the bridge and overstressing a bolt
ders: the British Army ordered troops to break step when crossing bridges
yanilgi: The deck didn't shake itself apart. The rhythmic load broke one weak bolt in a chain.
tartisma: The order to break step is still used today. Is an old rule still useful if we rarely see the danger?
basliklar: The Bridge That Made Soldiers Break Step
Why the Broughton Bridge Collapsed
sahneler: A suspension bridge near Manchester collapsed under marching soldiers.
The deck suddenly collapsed, and dozens fell into the river.
They had been marching perfectly in step.
The bridge began to bounce with their rhythm.
That rhythm concentrated stress on one weak bolt.
The bolt broke, and one end of the deck fell.
Nobody died, but the lesson stuck.
Soldiers have been ordered to break step on bridges ever since.
